q1: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS 'DISTINCT PRODUCTS' FROM PRODUCT)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) FROM PRODUCT)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT CUSTOMER_ID FROM CUSTOMER GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) = (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT PRODUCT_KEY) AS 'DISTINCT PRODUCTS' FROM PRODUCT)
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are semantically equivalent. The only difference is the alias given to the subquery result in Q2 (`AS 'DISTINCT PRODUCTS'`). Since the subquery returns a single scalar value, the alias has no impact on the comparison in the HAVING clause. Both queries select customer IDs who have purchased all distinct products in the PRODUCT table.
